title: SAP Concur to Business Central: Automating the Expense Journal Without Losing the Audit Check
summary: A practical Concur Business Central integration guide: automate the expense journal, keep a pre-posting audit check, and stop setting up beneficiaries twice.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Many finance teams export SAP Concur expense data, reshape it in Excel and import a journal into Business Central by hand because they want to audit before posting. A pre-posting validation layer keeps that audit while removing the rework, by checking mapping, dimensions, tax codes, duplicates and policy on every line and sending only exceptions to a person. Pair it with a single beneficiary master and bank file or API payments so employees and vendors are not set up twice.


If your organisation runs SAP Concur for claims and Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central for the general ledger, there is a good chance one person spends part of every month doing the same thing: downloading the Concur extract, opening it in Excel, re-ordering columns, fixing account codes and dimensions, and importing a journal into Business Central. Then they open the bank portal and key in reimbursements to employees whose bank details already exist somewhere else.


Ask why it is still manual and the answer is usually reasonable: “We want to check it before it hits the ledger.” That instinct is correct. The problem is that manual reshaping is a poor way to deliver that check. This guide explains how a Concur Business Central integration can automate the expense journal while keeping, and in fact strengthening, the human audit.


## What Is a Concur Business Central Integration?


A Concur Business Central integration is an automated connection that takes approved expense reports from SAP Concur and posts them as balanced journal entries in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, with the correct G/L accounts, dimensions and tax codes. A well-designed one also triggers or prepares employee reimbursement and supports reconciliation.


There is no single out-of-the-box answer. Concur produces accounting data through its Standard Accounting Extract (the “SAE file”) or through its financial integration APIs. Business Central accepts data through general journals, APIs, configuration packages and connectors. The integration is whatever sits between them, and the quality of that middle layer determines whether you keep an audit check or lose it.


## What Does the Manual Concur-to-Business Central Flow Look Like?


The typical manual flow has six or seven steps: run or download the Concur extract, open it in Excel, reshape columns and translate expense types to G/L accounts and dimensions, check totals, import into a Business Central general journal, review and post, then pay reimbursements separately through the bank portal and reconcile later.


Each step exists for a reason. The extract contains Concur codes, not Business Central account numbers. Cost centre or project values might be held in custom Concur fields that need translating into dimension codes. Tax treatment on foreign receipts needs a look. And because nothing validates the file automatically, the reviewer is the validation.


The second, quieter problem is beneficiary duplication. Employees and vendors who receive payments are set up once as employees or vendors in Business Central and again as beneficiaries in the bank portal. Payments are then either keyed one by one or uploaded from a file built by hand, and every payment is checked manually against the subledger.


## What Are the Risks of Reshaping Concur Exports in Excel?


The main risks are silent mapping errors, broken formulas, duplicate imports, inconsistent tax coding and a weak audit trail. Excel reshaping feels controlled because a person touches every row, but the person is checking their own transformation, and the steps they took are rarely recorded in a way an auditor can re-perform.


Specific failure modes finance teams report include:


- **Stale mapping.** A new Concur expense type is added, nobody updates the lookup table, and the line falls into a suspense or default account.
- **Dimension drift.** A cost centre is closed in Business Central but still selectable in Concur, so the import fails or, worse, posts to the wrong dimension.
- **Double imports.** The same extract is imported twice after a failed first attempt, and duplicates are only found at reconciliation. Our guide on[preventing duplicate invoices and payments](https://peakflo.co/blog/prevent-duplicate-invoices-payments-accounts-payable) covers the same pattern in AP.
- **Tax inconsistency.** Foreign receipts and non-claimable input tax are coded differently by different reviewers.
- **Bank detail mismatch.** The bank portal holds an older account number than the ERP, a classic source of failed or misdirected payments explored in our article on[vendor bank account errors and payment failures](https://peakflo.co/blog/vendor-bank-account-errors-payment-failures-ap-automation) .
- **Key-person dependency.** The spreadsheet logic lives in one person’s head and one person’s file.


None of these are solved by a more careful reviewer. They are solved by making the checks explicit and running them every time.


## What Are the Integration Options for Concur and Business Central?


There are four realistic options: consume the Concur Standard Accounting Extract file, use Concur’s financial integration APIs, build flows in middleware such as Power Automate or Workato, or use a finance automation platform that handles extract, validation, posting and payment together. The right choice depends on volume, entity count and in-house skills.


**1. Standard Accounting Extract (SAE file).** Concur’s SAE is a delimited flat file containing approved, accounting-ready expense data, typically delivered by SFTP or retrieved through the[Concur Extracts API](https://developer.concur.com/api-reference/common/extracts/v1.extracts.html) . It is stable and widely used, but it still needs translation into Business Central’s structure.


**2. Concur financial integration APIs.** Concur’s financial integration service exposes posting documents through APIs and lets the receiving system acknowledge what has been posted. SAP’s[financial integration use case documentation](https://developer.concur.com/api-reference/financial-integration/v4.financial-integration-service-use-cases.html) shows how expense postings map to accounting records. This is more robust than file-based transfer but needs development effort.


**3. Middleware and low-code.** Microsoft’s[Business Central connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/dynamicssmbsaas/) lets Power Automate create and update records, and Microsoft documents[using Business Central in Power Automate flows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/across-how-use-financials-data-source-flow) . Integration platforms such as[Workato’s Concur connector](https://www.workato.com/integrations/concur) offer similar building blocks. Middleware is flexible, but validation logic tends to get buried inside flows that only their author understands.


**4. Finance automation platform.** A platform with native Business Central integration ingests the Concur output, applies mapping and validation rules in a configurable rules engine, routes exceptions for review, posts journals and pays reimbursements from one beneficiary master. This option trades build effort for subscription cost.


The table below compares the manual flow with a well-designed automated flow, step by step.


Step Manual flow today Automated flow with pre-posting validation


Get approved expenses Download Concur extract by hand SAE file or API pulled on schedule


Translate codes VLOOKUPs in Excel Maintained mapping table applied automatically


Check dimensions and tax Reviewer eyeballs each line Rules validate every line; failures flagged


Detect duplicates Rely on memory and totals Report ID and line hash checked against posted history


Import journal Manual configuration package or paste into journal Journal created via API in a named batch


Review Reviewer re-checks entire file Reviewer sees only exceptions, with receipt image


Post Manual post Auto-post clean batch after approval, or post on reviewer sign-off


Pay reimbursements Key or upload into bank portal with separate beneficiaries Bank file or API from single beneficiary master


Reconcile Match bank lines manually Auto-match statement lines to payments and ledger entries


## How Do You Preserve the Audit Check With Pre-Posting Validation?


You preserve the audit check by turning what the reviewer does in Excel into explicit validation rules that run on every line before posting, then routing only the lines that fail to a person. The human still approves what goes to the ledger, but spends time on exceptions rather than re-reading clean data.


This is the key design decision. Teams often reject automation because they believe it means posting blind. It does not have to. A pre-posting validation layer is a staging step between Concur and Business Central where each line is tested, scored and either passed or held.


Design it in three tiers:


- **Hard stops.** Lines that cannot post: unmapped expense type, invalid or blocked dimension value, missing tax code, journal out of balance. These are held and returned.
- **Review flags.** Lines that can post but need a human look: amount above a threshold, possible duplicate, policy exception approved in Concur, foreign currency receipt, weekend or holiday spend.
- **Clean lines.** Everything else, which posts automatically or on one-click batch approval.


The logic for a single line can be expressed simply.


```text
FOR each expense line in approved Concur batch:
IF expense_type has no G/L mapping          -> HOLD (hard stop)
IF dimension value blocked or invalid in BC -> HOLD (hard stop)
IF tax code missing for taxable type        -> HOLD (hard stop)
IF report_id + line_id already posted       -> HOLD (duplicate)
IF amount > review_threshold                -> FLAG for reviewer
IF policy_exception = TRUE                  -> FLAG for reviewer
ELSE                                        -> PASS
IF batch total debits = credits AND no HOLD lines:
create journal batch in Business Central -> post on reviewer sign-off
```


The reviewer now signs off a batch knowing every line has passed the same checks they used to perform by hand, and they can see exactly which lines were flagged and why. That is a stronger audit trail than a reworked spreadsheet, because the rules, the results and the approver are all recorded.


The validation checks worth implementing first are summarised below.


Validation check What it catches Typical action


Expense type mapping exists New or renamed Concur expense types Hard stop; update mapping table


Dimension value valid and not blocked Closed cost centres, wrong project or grant codes Hard stop; correct in Concur or override with approval


Dimension combination allowed Project posted against wrong department Hard stop


Tax code present and consistent with expense type Missing or wrong VAT/GST treatment Hard stop or flag


Duplicate report or line Re-sent extracts, double imports Hard stop


Amount over threshold High-value claims needing a second look Flag for reviewer


Policy exception or late claim Out-of-policy approvals Flag for reviewer


Journal in balance Rounding or currency errors Hard stop


Employee or vendor exists in BC New joiners not yet set up Hard stop; create from master


## How Should You Map Concur Expense Types to Business Central G/L Accounts and Dimensions?


Map each Concur expense type to exactly one Business Central G/L account and tax posting group, and map each Concur allocation or custom field to a Business Central dimension. Keep the mapping in one maintained table, owned by finance, with a change log, rather than scattered across Excel formulas.


Start with your[chart of accounts in Business Central](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-setup-chart-accounts) and your[dimension setup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-dimensions) . Then work through Concur’s expense type list and allocation fields. Tax treatment should be driven by[VAT posting setup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-setup-vat) in Business Central, which is also used for GST in markets such as Singapore.


The following example shows how a mapping table might look for a non-profit or professional services organisation.


Concur expense type Business Central G/L account Tax posting group Dimension source


Airfare 6110 Travel - Air Exempt / zero-rated Department from employee; Project from Concur allocation


Hotel 6120 Travel - Accommodation Standard-rated or foreign (non-claimable) Department; Project


Meals - Staff Travel 6130 Travel - Meals Standard-rated Department; Project


Client or Donor Entertainment 6210 Entertainment Non-claimable Department; Programme or grant


Conference Fees 6310 Training and Conferences Standard-rated Department; Programme


Mobile and Internet 6410 Communications Standard-rated Department


Mileage 6140 Travel - Mileage Out of scope Department; Project


Three practical tips. First, derive as many dimensions as possible from the employee record rather than asking claimants to choose, which reduces errors at source; our[comparison of automated and manual GL coding](https://peakflo.co/blog/automated-vs-manual-gl-coding-comparison) explains why. Second, use Business Central’s default dimensions and blocked dimension values so invalid combinations fail validation rather than posting. Third, decide whether to post at line level or summarised by account and dimension; line level gives better drill-down, summarised keeps the ledger lighter.


## How Do You Get Data Into Business Central Without Manual Imports?


Use Business Central’s APIs or a connector to create lines directly in a named general journal batch, rather than importing a file by hand. The journal remains the familiar review surface, so your team can still open, inspect and post it, but nobody has to build or paste the file.


Business Central’s[general journals](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/ui-work-general-journals) support posting to G/L accounts, vendors, employees and bank accounts, with dimensions on each line. Many teams currently use[configuration packages](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/across-import-data-configuration-packages) to import journal lines from Excel; that works, but it is still a manual file step. An API-based approach creates the same lines programmatically, tagged with the Concur report ID so every posted entry can be traced back to its source report and receipt.


If you want a formal approval before posting, Business Central’s[approval workflows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/across-how-use-approval-workflows) can be applied to general journal batches, so the reviewer’s sign-off is captured inside the ERP itself.


## How Should Employee Reimbursements and Beneficiaries Be Handled?


Reimbursements should be paid from a single beneficiary master, with employee and vendor bank details held once and pushed to the bank by file or API, never re-entered in the bank portal. That removes double data entry, eliminates mismatched bank details, and means one controlled change process governs every beneficiary.


Today, many teams set up each employee or vendor twice: once in Business Central and once in the bank portal. That doubles the work of every onboarding and every bank detail change, and it creates two versions of the truth that drift apart over time.


A better design:


- **One master.** Bank details live in Business Central (or the payment platform synchronised with it) and nowhere else.
- **Controlled changes.** Any change to bank details requires verification and a second approver, logged against the record.
- **Generated payments.** Payment journals in Business Central produce a bank file using the[electronic payment and bank data conversion features](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-make-payments-with-bank-data-conversion-service-or-sepa-credit-transfer) , or a payment platform sends payments through bank APIs. The bank portal is used only to authorise, not to key.
- **Proof of payment.** Remittance advice goes to the employee or vendor automatically.


For more on handling staff claims across programmes and claimant types, see our guide to[expense and reimbursement management for non-profit organisations](https://peakflo.co/blog/expense-reimbursement-management-non-profit-organizations) .


## How Do You Reconcile Reimbursements Back in Business Central?


Reconcile by matching each bank statement line to the reimbursement payment and its employee or vendor ledger entries in Business Central, ideally automatically. When payments are generated from the ERP with consistent references, statement matching becomes a rules exercise rather than a monthly hunt through the bank portal.


Business Central supports[automatic application of payments and bank reconciliation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/receivables-apply-payments-auto-reconcile-bank-accounts) , which works best when payment references are predictable. Use the Concur report ID or a batch reference in the payment description so each bank line points back to a specific claim. At month-end, reviewers should only need to look at unmatched lines, open employee balances and any reimbursement returned by the bank.

## Our Verdict: Should You Automate the Concur Expense Journal?


Yes, if the manual process is consuming real time each month or creating posting errors, because a pre-posting validation layer lets you automate without giving up the audit check. The one case to wait is when claim volumes are very low and the reshaping takes minutes, not hours.


### Automate now if


- Reshaping and importing the Concur extract takes more than a few hours a month.
- You have had mapping errors, duplicate imports or suspense account clean-ups in the last year.
- Beneficiaries are maintained in both Business Central and the bank portal.
- One person owns the spreadsheet logic and nobody else can run it.


### Start with mapping and validation only if


- Volumes are moderate and the journal import itself is quick.
- Your main concern is consistency of G/L, dimension and tax coding.
- You want to prove the rules before letting anything auto-post.


### Wait if


- You process only a handful of claims a month and reshaping takes minutes.
- Your Concur expense types and Business Central dimensions are about to be redesigned.

## Conclusion


Keeping Concur-to-Business Central posting manual “so we can audit it” mixes up two different things: the audit and the reshaping. The audit is valuable. The reshaping is not, and it actually weakens the audit by hiding the logic in a spreadsheet.


A good Concur Business Central integration separates them. Extraction and posting become automatic; mapping, dimension, tax, duplicate and policy checks become explicit rules; and reviewers spend their time on genuine exceptions. Add a single beneficiary master and bank-integrated payments, and you remove the second manual process in the chain as well.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Does SAP Concur have a native integration with Business Central?


There is no single native, out-of-the-box connector that covers mapping, validation, posting and reimbursement for every organisation. Most teams connect the two using the Concur Standard Accounting Extract or financial integration APIs, combined with middleware, custom development or a finance automation platform with native Business Central integration.


### What is the Concur SAE file?


The Standard Accounting Extract (SAE) is a delimited flat file generated by SAP Concur containing approved, accounting-ready expense data such as employee, expense type, amounts, tax and allocation fields. It is typically delivered by SFTP or retrieved through the Concur Extracts API, then transformed into the format the ERP needs.


### How do I import Concur expenses into a Business Central general journal?


You can import lines manually using a configuration package or Excel, or create them automatically through Business Central APIs or a connector. Either way, lines should carry a G/L or employee account, dimensions, tax posting group and a reference back to the Concur report ID for traceability.


### Can I automate the Concur journal and still review before posting?


Yes. Add a pre-posting validation layer that checks every line for mapping, dimensions, tax codes, duplicates and policy, then hold or flag failing lines for review. The reviewer signs off a batch knowing every line passed the same checks, and only investigates exceptions.


### How should Concur expense types map to Business Central G/L accounts?


Each Concur expense type should map to exactly one G/L account and one tax posting group, held in a single maintained mapping table owned by finance. Allocation fields such as cost centre, project or grant map to Business Central dimensions, with as many as possible derived from the employee record.


### What validation checks should run before posting Concur expenses?


Start with expense type mapping exists, dimension value valid and not blocked, allowed dimension combinations, tax code present and consistent, duplicate report or line detection, journal balance, employee or vendor exists in Business Central, amount thresholds and policy exception flags.


### How do I stop setting up employees and vendors twice in the ERP and bank portal?


Hold bank details in one master, either Business Central or a payment platform synchronised with it, and generate payments to the bank by file or API. Use the bank portal only to authorise payments, and route every bank detail change through a verified, approved process.


### Can Power Automate handle the Concur to Business Central integration?


Power Automate can move data and create Business Central records using the Business Central connector, and it suits simple, low-volume flows. Validation logic, mapping tables, exception queues and audit logging need careful design, and complex flows can become hard to maintain if only one person understands them.


### How are VAT or GST codes handled for Concur expenses in Business Central?


Business Central uses VAT posting setup, which also serves GST in markets such as Singapore. Map each Concur expense type to a VAT product posting group and validate that taxable lines carry a tax code, with foreign or non-claimable receipts handled by a specific posting group.


### How do I reconcile employee reimbursements in Business Central?


Generate reimbursement payments from Business Central payment journals with consistent references such as the Concur report ID, then use automatic payment application and bank reconciliation to match statement lines to employee or vendor ledger entries. Review only unmatched lines and open balances at month-end.


### Should expense lines be posted in detail or summarised in Business Central?


Line-level posting gives full drill-down from the ledger to each claim and receipt, which helps audits and grant reporting. Summarised posting by account and dimension keeps the ledger lighter. Many organisations post at line level for project or grant-funded spend and summarise routine categories.
